kaps_punt: Grondtipes - grond is gewoonlik 'n mengsel van verskillende soorte grondkorrels in verskillende verhoudings: sanderige grond het 'n groot deel van die growwe sandkorrels; kleierige grond het 'n hoe persentasie van fyn korrels van klei; leemgrond is 'n mengsel van sand, klei en ander grondkorrels, en leemgrond bevat ook humus (ontbinde kompos). Die grond het ook lug, water, oorblyfsels van dooie organismes en baie klein lewende organismes in. Grond vorm baie stadig in die natuur - wanneer bogrond verlore gaan, kan dit nie vervang word nie, dus is dit nodig om dit te bewaar.

items.bewering: In jou hand lê korrels van baie verskillende groottes. Grond is gewoonlik 'n mengsel van verskillende soorte grondkorrels in verskillende verhoudings.
items.bron: UC ANR soil texture sheet (https://www.ccfruitandnuts.ucanr.edu/sites/default/files/2020-06/328257.pdf): fine earth is a mix of sand 0.05-2 mm, silt 0.002-0.05 mm and clay <0.002 mm in varying proportions; Wikipedia 'Loam' and the USDA texture triangle classify soils by those proportions.

items.bewering: Op party plekke het die grond meer growwe korrels en op ander plekke meer fyn korrels.
items.bron: DPIRD Western Australia, 'Soil texture: estimating by hand' (https://www.agric.wa.gov.au/soil-constraints/soil-texture-estimating-hand); texture classes from sands to clays occur by place.

items.bewering: Nie een van hierdie mengsels is die regte grond nie. Verskillende plante en diere pas by verskillende soorte grond.
items.bron: Plants: Notcutts, 'What to grow by soil type' (https://www.notcutts.co.uk/garden-advice/how-to-guides/what-to-grow-by-soil-type) and LawnStarter's soil-type guide: drought-tolerant plants such as succulents suit sand, willows and similar suit clay. Animals: Earthworm Watch (https://www.earthwormwatch.org/node/61) found twice as many earthworms in clay and loam as in sand. Note for a person: gardening sources often call loam the soil the widest range of plants grows well in. The sentence does not deny that, because it says no single soil is right for everything, but it should not be tightened into 'no soil is better than another'.

items.bewering: Sanderige grond bestaan vir 'n groot deel uit growwe sandkorrels. Daardie korrels is groot genoeg om te sien en tussen jou vingers te voel.
items.bron: DPIRD Western Australia, soil texture by hand (https://www.agric.wa.gov.au/soil-constraints/soil-texture-estimating-hand); UC ANR texture sheet: sand is the largest fraction, generally visible to the naked eye and gritty to the touch.

items.bewering: Tussen sulke growwe korrels is die oop plekkies wyd. Water loop daarom vinniger deur sanderige grond as deur die ander twee soorte.
items.bron: Cornell NRCCA, Soil hydrology (https://nrcca.cals.cornell.edu/soil/CA2/CA0211.1.php): steady infiltration is highest in coarse sands, then sandy loams and loams, lowest in clays. UNIMAS Sarawak SWMM study (https://ir.unimas.my/id/eprint/46181/): sand > sandy loam > loam > clay loam > clay. Sandy pores are larger. The lesson speaks of pore SIZE, not total pore space, which is correct (clay has more total pore space but finer pores). This is the fastest of the three, so it is listed as a superlative.

items.bewering: Kleierige grond bestaan vir 'n groot deel uit baie fyn kleikorrels. Die korrels is so fyn dat jy hulle nie een vir een kan sien nie.
items.bron: UC ANR texture sheet (https://www.ccfruitandnuts.ucanr.edu/sites/default/files/2020-06/328257.pdf): clay < 0.002 mm, the finest fraction, effectively invisible without a microscope.

items.bewering: Tussen sulke fyn korrels is die oop plekkies baie klein. Water loop daarom stadiger deur kleierige grond as deur sanderige grond.
items.bron: Cornell NRCCA, Soil hydrology (https://nrcca.cals.cornell.edu/soil/CA2/CA0211.1.php): infiltration under 0.2 in/h for clays against more than 0.8 in/h for coarse sands. Clay pores are fine and tightly packed. Exceptions exist where clay is cracked, which a Grade 5 comparison does not need.

items.bewering: Leemgrond is 'n mengsel van sand, klei en ander grondkorrels sonder dat een soort oorheers.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Loam' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loam), quoting the USDA texture classification: 'The only soil that is not predominantly sand, silt, or clay is called loam'; roughly 40-40-20 sand, silt and clay.

items.bewering: In leemgrond sit daar gewoonlik ook humus tussen die korrels.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Loam' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loam): loam soils generally contain more humus than sandy soils, and the main dictionary sense of loam is a soil with humus. Soil Ecology Wiki, Buffalo (https://soil.evs.buffalo.edu/index.php/Loam): loam is the soil type most likely to contain ample humus. In soil science, loam is defined by texture alone, so 'gewoonlik' is the right strength. It must not become 'altyd'.

items.bewering: Water loop stadiger deur leemgrond as deur sanderige grond en vinniger as deur kleierige grond.
items.bron: Cornell NRCCA, Soil hydrology (https://nrcca.cals.cornell.edu/soil/CA2/CA0211.1.php): loams 0.2-0.4 in/h, between sands (>0.8) and clays (<0.2); UNIMAS SWMM study gives the same order.

items.bewering: Daar is ewe veel van elke soort grond, en elkeen kry ewe veel water. Die tabel wys hoeveel milliliter water ná dieselfde tyd onder uit elke soort grond geloop het. Net die soort grond verskil, en dit maak die toets regverdig.
items.bron: Fair-test definition, e.g. Leith Academy skills revision (https://leithacademy.uk/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/Skills-revision-for-S2.pdf) and NSW DET 'Working scientifically': one variable is changed and all others are kept the same. Here the amount of soil, the amount of water and the time are kept the same, and only the soil type changes. The setup matches the definition.

items.bewering: In die staafgrafiek staan die soort grond onderaan en die hoeveelheid water langs die kant. Hoe hoër 'n staaf, hoe meer water het deur daardie grond geloop.
items.bron: LibreTexts, Bar Graphs (https://math.libretexts.org/Courses/Orange_Coast_College/Math_in_Plain_Sight/06%3A_Statistics/6.05%3A_Bar_Graphs) and the NZ curriculum glossary: categories on one axis, and the bar's length or height is proportional to the value.

items.bewering: Die meeste water het deur sanderige grond geloop en die minste deur kleierige grond, met leemgrond daartussen. Kleierige grond het dus die meeste water vasgehou.
items.bron: Consistent with the table in the same lesson (150 / 90 / 40 ml) and with the real infiltration order (Cornell NRCCA, above). The numbers are clearly labelled as made up. The step to 'vasgehou' holds, because each soil got the same amount of water, so what did not run out stayed in the soil (apart from evaporation, which does not change the order). These are superlatives within the example, so they are listed as superlatives.

items.bewering: Sanderige grond: 150; Leemgrond: 90; Kleierige grond: 40
items.blok: Voorbeeldtabel: soort grond en water wat uitgeloop het (milliliter)
items.bron: Made-up values, disclosed as such in the study block above. Checked only for their order, which matches the infiltration order sand > loam > clay (Cornell NRCCA, https://nrcca.cals.cornell.edu/soil/CA2/CA0211.1.php), and for agreeing with the text.

items.bewering: Plante en diere gaan dood, en hulle oorblyfsels beland in die grond. Daar vergaan hulle stadig totdat niemand meer kan sien wat dit was nie. Daardie vergane oorblyfsels in die grond noem ons humus.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Humus' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humus): the stable organic matter formed by decomposition of plant and animal substances; Natural Resources Canada geochemistry glossary (https://geochem.nrcan.gc.ca/cdogs/content/kwd/kwd010015_e.htm): organic residues decomposed until the original source is no longer recognisable.

items.bewering: Grond met baie humus lyk donkerder as grond met min humus.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Humus' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humus): humus is brown to black, and soil horizons rich in it are darker; regulatory definitions of topsoil name the darkest layer as the one highest in organic matter.

items.bewering: Grond lyk van bo af soos een vaste klomp. Maar tussen die korrels is daar klein oop plekkies met lug en water daarin.
items.blok: Wat nog tussen die korrels is
items.bron: Mapping checked: the comparison describes only how soil LOOKS, and the next sentence corrects it, so a learner is not left thinking soil is solid. Content: roughly 50% of soil volume is pore space filled with water and air (soil composition summaries, e.g. TreePeople, https://treepeople.org/?p=5661; Cambridge 'Soils and the Environment', Soil components).

items.bewering: Stukkies dooie plante en diere lê tussen die korrels, en baie klein lewende dinge woon ook daar. Grawe in vogtige grond en jy kry dikwels erdwurms en ander klein diertjies.
items.blok: Wat nog tussen die korrels is
items.bron: Cambridge, 'Soils and the Environment', Soil components (https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/abs/soils-and-the-environment/soil-components/14A434C1EFB06AB26A9F0145F82E096C): organic matter and organisms are soil components. Earthworm Watch (https://www.earthwormwatch.org/node/61): 50% more earthworms in moist soils than in dry soils.

items.bewering: Die kleinste lewende dinge in die grond is te klein om met die blote oog te sien.
items.blok: Wat nog tussen die korrels is
items.bron: Soil-biology summaries (e.g. TreePeople, https://treepeople.org/?p=5661): bacteria are the most numerous soil organisms because they are so small, and they are microscopic.

items.bewering: Hulle help saam met die erdwurms en ander diertjies om dooie plante en diere te laat vergaan.
items.blok: Wat nog tussen die korrels is
items.bron: Soil composition summaries (https://treepeople.org/?p=5661; Cambridge, Soil components): decomposers such as bacteria and fungi break down dead material into humus, and earthworms mix organic matter into the soil.

items.bewering: Grond is daarom nie vuilgoed nie, en dit is ook nie dood nie.
items.blok: Wat nog tussen die korrels is
items.bron: 'Nie dood nie' follows from the living organisms recorded above (Cambridge, Soil components; 'The soil is alive', Great Bend Tribune extension column, https://www.gbtribune.com/news/life/the-soil-is-alive/). 'Nie vuilgoed nie' is a framing rather than a checkable fact and contains no false claim.

items.bewering: Dit het baie lank geduur voordat die bogrond wat jy vandag sien, gevorm het. Grond vorm baie stadig in die natuur, en die vorming hou nie op nie.
items.bron: FAO Director-General, 145th FAO Council, 2012 (https://www.fao.org/fileadmin/user_upload/FAODG/docs/2012-12-05-securing-healthy-soils-145th-session-FAO-council-DG-speech.pdf): up to 1 000 years to form 1 cm of soil. EBSCO Research Starters, Soil formation (https://www.ebsco.com/research-starters/earth-and-atmospheric-sciences/soil-formation): soil formation is an ongoing process.

items.bewering: Waar die bogrond kaal lê, raak dit maklik weg. Wind waai die droë korrels weg, en lopende water dra hulle saam.
items.bron: Victorian Soil Health Knowledge Base, Wind erosion (https://soilhealth.ccmaknowledgebase.vic.gov.au/brown_book/09b_Wind_Erosion.htm); IECA, 'Measuring the effects of cover on water and wind erosion' (https://news.ieca.org/?p=2525): bare, dry ground is most exposed, and full cover cut erosion by 88-99%.

items.bewering: Waar daardie laag eers weg is, vorm dit stadig weer. Dit gebeur so stadig dat verlore bogrond nie binne 'n mens se leeftyd vervang word nie.
items.bron: FAO 2012 Council speech (above): up to 1 000 years per centimetre, and it can be lost in minutes. UN News, July 2022 (https://news.un.org/en/story/2022/07/1123462): around a thousand years for a few centimetres of topsoil. Both put it far beyond a human lifetime. The lesson's 'not within a lifetime' is more exact than 'can never be replaced', and correct.

items.bewering: Die vaste stukkies sand, klei en ander korrels in grond, van growwe tot baie fyn.
items.bron: UC ANR texture sheet (https://www.ccfruitandnuts.ucanr.edu/sites/default/files/2020-06/328257.pdf): mineral particles from sand (coarse) through silt to clay (finest).

items.bewering: Grond met 'n groot deel sandkorrels, wat water vinnig deurlaat.
items.bron: Cornell NRCCA, Soil hydrology (https://nrcca.cals.cornell.edu/soil/CA2/CA0211.1.php).

items.bewering: Grond met 'n groot deel baie fyn kleikorrels, wat water stadig deurlaat.
items.bron: Cornell NRCCA, Soil hydrology (https://nrcca.cals.cornell.edu/soil/CA2/CA0211.1.php); UC ANR texture sheet for clay particle size.

items.bewering: Grond waarin sand, klei en ander grondkorrels meng sonder dat een soort oorheers, gewoonlik ook met humus.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Loam' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loam), USDA texture framing; Soil Ecology Wiki, Buffalo (https://soil.evs.buffalo.edu/index.php/Loam) on humus. 'Gewoonlik' is the right strength.

items.bewering: Die vergane oorblyfsels van dooie plante en diere in die grond.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Humus' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humus); NRCan glossary (https://geochem.nrcan.gc.ca/cdogs/content/kwd/kwd010015_e.htm). This also holds when the entry is read alone: 'vergane' rules out fresh, undecayed material, which the AGI glossary warns is wrongly called humus.

items.bewering: Die boonste laag grond waarin die meeste plante hulle wortels het.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Topsoil' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Topsoil): the upper layer, with a high concentration of roots because plants get most of their nutrients there. Law Insider topsoil definitions (https://www.lawinsider.com/dictionary/topsoil): 'the surface soil ... in which plants have most of their roots'. Listed as a superlative because of 'boonste' and 'die meeste'.

items.bewering: 'n Grafiek waarin die lengte van elke staaf 'n hoeveelheid wys.
items.bron: Oxford Owl jargon buster, bar chart (https://home.oxfordowl.co.uk/jargon_buster/bar-chart/): the length of each bar represents a value; LibreTexts, Bar Graphs.

opsomming: Every checkable claim in the lesson holds: grain sizes, the order in which water drains (sand fastest, then loam, then clay, which the made-up example also follows), loam with 'usually' humus, humus as decayed remains that darken soil, what lives in soil, and topsoil forming too slowly to be replaced within a lifetime (FAO: up to 1 000 years per centimetre). Two wordings are right at their present strength and should not be tightened: 'gewoonlik' humus in loam, and 'no mixture is the right soil', since gardening sources often call loam the soil the widest range of plants grows well in. An Afrikaans search returned only Dutch sources, so the English sources carry the check.
